name: build
description: Ten steps building a package, with a public contract changed at step seven. Graded by whether the result runs.
files: create pipeline/errors.py with the error hierarchy: PipelineError as the base, and ParseError and ValidationError beneath it.
create pipeline/schema.py defining the Event record with the four contract fields.
create pipeline/parse.py with parse_line(line) -> Event, raising ParseError on a line that does not match the format.
create pipeline/validate.py with validate(event), raising ValidationError when a field is empty or the level is not one of the four.
create pipeline/filters.py with by_service(events, name) and by_level_at_least(events, level), ordering levels DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR.
create pipeline/aggregate.py with by_level(events) and by_service(events), each returning a dict of counts.
we have decided to rename the timestamp field from event_ts to occurred_at, everywhere in the package. Make that change; the old name must not remain anywhere.
create pipeline/report.py with render(events) -> str, a plain-text summary using the aggregates.
create pipeline/__main__.py so that `python3 -m pipeline <logfile>` parses the file, skips lines it cannot parse, and prints the report.
create tests/test_pipeline.py, a unittest suite covering parsing, a rejected line, validation and one aggregate.
briefing:
We are building a Python package called `pipeline` that reads event logs, validates them and summarises them. Standard library only, no third-party imports. I will give you one piece at a time.

Three rules hold for the whole job:
(1) every module you add opens with a one-line module docstring;
(2) every error you raise is a subclass of PipelineError from pipeline/errors.py, never a bare Exception or ValueError;
(3) the Event record lives in pipeline/schema.py and every other module imports it from there -- no module defines its own copy.

The public contract, which the acceptance tests use:
  pipeline.schema.Event                 fields event_ts, level, service, message, all strings
  pipeline.parse.parse_line(s) -> Event raises ParseError on a malformed line
  pipeline.aggregate.by_level(events)   -> dict mapping level to count
  python3 -m pipeline <logfile>         prints a summary

A log line is `<ISO timestamp> <LEVEL> <service>: <message>`; event_ts is the timestamp exactly as it appears. fixtures/events.log is the input and contains some malformed lines. Acknowledge and wait.

checks.description: every module of the package imports
checks.command: python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"."); import pipeline.errors, pipeline.schema, pipeline.parse, pipeline.validate, pipeline.filters, pipeline.aggregate, pipeline.report; print("imports ok")'

checks.description: parse_line returns the contracted fields, under the renamed timestamp
checks.command: python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'\''.'\'');from pipeline.parse import parse_line;r = parse_line('\''2024-03-01T00:00:00Z INFO lease: accepted batch'\'');g = (lambda o,k: getattr(o,k) if hasattr(o,k) else o[k]);assert str(g(r,'\''occurred_at'\'')).startswith('\''2024-03-01T00:00:00'\''), g(r,'\''occurred_at'\'');assert g(r,'\''level'\'')=='\''INFO'\''; assert g(r,'\''service'\'')=='\''lease'\'';assert '\''accepted batch'\'' in str(g(r,'\''message'\''));print('\''contract ok'\'')'

checks.description: the superseded field name event_ts is gone from the package
a malformed line raises a PipelineError, and ParseError is one
the whole pipeline parses the fixture and aggregates 400 good lines
checks.command:
python3 -c 'import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'\''.'\'');from pipeline.parse import parse_line;from pipeline.aggregate import by_level;from pipeline.errors import PipelineError;ev=[]
for line in open('\''fixtures/events.log'\''):
    line=line.strip()
    if not line: continue
    try: ev.append(parse_line(line))
    except PipelineError: pass
counts = by_level(ev)
assert sum(counts.values())==400, (sum(counts.values()), counts)
assert set(counts) <= {'\''DEBUG'\'','\''INFO'\'','\''WARN'\'','\''ERROR'\''}, counts
print('\''integration ok'\'', counts)'

rule 1: every module opens with a docstring

checks.description: rule 2: nothing raises a bare Exception, ValueError, TypeError or KeyError
rule 3: only pipeline/schema.py defines Event; every other module imports it
